title: Infrastructure Gaps Test Pakistan’s Flagship CPEC Industrial Zone, Field Survey Finds
gist: Allama Iqbal Industrial City, the first CPEC-priority Special Economic Zone in Faisalabad, has drawn over 327 billion rupees ($1.2 billion) in committed investment and allotted 223 of 424 plots, but a field survey finds no piped potable water network, unfinished sewerage and no funded Combined Effluent Treatment Plant.

insights.claim: Allama Iqbal Industrial City, the first Special Economic Zone prioritized under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, has drawn more than 327 billion rupees ($1.2 billion) in committed investment and allotted 223 of 424 planned plots.
insights.speaker: Mujtaba Arshad
insights.so_what: Committed capital is substantial, but only about half the plots are allotted; watch conversion of commitments into operating capacity.
insights.quote: has drawn more than 327 billion rupees ($1.2 billion) in committed investment and allotted 223 of 424 planned plots

insights.claim: Basic infrastructure at the CPEC flagship zone has not kept pace with investment, and zone management itself lists the resulting gaps among its most urgent priorities.
insights.speaker: Mujtaba Arshad
insights.so_what: Infrastructure shortfalls raise operating costs for tenants, including Chinese JVs, and can slow CPEC industrial relocation.

insights.claim: There is no zone-wide piped potable water network at Allama Iqbal Industrial City; firms rely on self-boring, drilling and managing their own wells.
insights.speaker: Mujtaba Arshad
insights.so_what: Self-supplied groundwater adds capex and long-term resource risk for water-intensive industries such as textiles.

insights.claim: Sewerage at the zone is still under construction and no Combined Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) has been funded, leaving firms to manage industrial wastewater largely on their own.
insights.speaker: Mujtaba Arshad
insights.so_what: Lack of effluent treatment is an environmental-compliance risk for export-oriented tenants facing buyer ESG standards.

insights.claim: The 3,966-acre zone along the M-4 Motorway is administered by FIEDMC; the survey covered FIEDMC and four operating firms, including a China-Pakistan joint venture, and is diagnostic rather than statistically representative.
insights.speaker: Mujtaba Arshad
insights.so_what: Findings are indicative, not comprehensive; treat as a qualitative red flag on SEZ execution.
